subject: Aerial surveys with different types of windows

messages.author: 404e5be3b58c8519
messages.subject: Aerial surveys with different types of windows
parts:
Dear all,I am seeking guidance on my analyses of marine mammal aerial survey
data in Distance 6.0 R2. I have two years worth of data at my disposal and
two types of aircrafts were used : either one fitted with bubble windows or
one fitted with flat windows. It is my understanding that these two types of
platforms will surely give distinct view-fields both on a vertical and a
horizontal axis (as a result for example the blind strip under the plane
will be more or less wide), so I thought it would be legitimate to analyze
the related subsets of my data separately. Is this a good approach ? I want
estimates for each year - should I rather run my analyses on the data pooled
over surveys (i.e regardless of window type) for each year ? Does it depend
on the number of observations closer to the trackline obtained one or the
other type of platform ?
Moreover, the ultimate goal of my work will be to yield daily estimates (by
post-stratifying by day, number of detections per stratum permitting) that
will later be integrated in a migration count model. Following example 8.6
("House wren densities") p 361-366 of Buckland et al. 2001 it seemed to me
that running analyses on an entire dataset using different candidate models
to start with, then choosing the best one and possibly relying on that model
to post stratify was acceptable. Do you agree ? The thing is that I have
(for various motives) 3 right truncation distances (largest observation, 13
km and 5 km) and several left truncation distances (contingent upon the type
of window used) to test. This added to different combination of models +
model selection procedures, I end up with tens (if not more) of analyses to
consider. I fear this might be too much and as a consequence that I might
not be thinking of this all the right way. Any suggestion(s) on how to
proceed ?
Any help, guidance, advice, comments or corrections will be most welcome.
Warm thanks in advance for your input,
Phil

messages.author: 5140016d70f6ba82
messages.subject: Re: Aerial surveys with different types of windows
parts:
It is possible to handle both platforms simultaneously with different
blind spots but not in the existing code. Thus I suggest that you left
truncate all the data for the maximum value from the flat windows, pool
all the data and look at platform as a possible covariate for
differences in detection probability using the MCDS engine.

With regard to the migration count, not sure how that fits into the wren
example. Also, you'll need to translate the area you sampled into time
based on average speed of migration to work in the migration idea.
Presumably they are all travelling in the same direction.

--jeff
